items.title: Bill Huntington and Charlie Suhor Interview, 1992-04-06
items.q: kind of in a Doug Watkins, early Ray Brown mode.

ctx.x: Yeah. Well, he drove all the better drummers away because by that time I was into my English teaching career and he pissed them off so badly that they wouldn't work with him anymore.

But another thing he did. And this goes back to it's very important in New Orleans to have outside influences because what happens, like in the case of Maus, you get these outside influences, they come to the city, Bill Evans is another example, they develop. And they develop, it's a give and take, it's a compromise with the city. They absorb things from the city and the city absorbs things from them. And I think that connection is really important. Anyway, it's kind of New York in a way. It's kind of what's been…
